title: Ember native launch, lineage choice, corpus access and useful operation
authority: Delivered founder-public envelope75386 assigns launch-path synthesis
intended_outcome: A user launches the correct host binary, activates the current authorized Ember lineage or creates a fresh one, and operates training, inference, evaluation and data sourcing without writing dispatch code. Initial ML/CS/SE/DS specialization supports verifiable improvements to Ember itself. Minimize measured time to useful competence without changing existing acceptance requirements.

selected_approach.recommendation: Expose one native operation service through the useful CLI first and a minimal GUI using the same commands, state and evidence. Reuse verified runtime components. Keep UI construction independent from model-development capability.

alternatives.approach: Wrap existing manual dispatch entry points as a transition
alternatives.tradeoff: Can shorten first operator path if the application owns invocation and custody, but each unintegrated operation remains explicitly unproved.

alternatives.approach: Shared native service with thin CLI and minimal GUI
alternatives.tradeoff: One owner for lineage, operations and data identity; UI can stay small while the runtime becomes demonstrable. Recommended.

alternatives.approach: Build a full GUI and separate operational backend
alternatives.tradeoff: Adds implementation and duplicated control paths before useful operation; no evidence presently justifies that cost.

selected_approach.implementation_choice: Exact modules and reuse decisions remain with runtime owner/CLI owner/projection implementer in their assigned scope; this document creates no implementation branch or runtime allocation.

claim_outcomes.meaning: The application itself completes the requested operation with correct lineage, inputs, process identity and terminal evidence. A window, command list, queue acknowledgement or source implementation alone is insufficient.

The selected checkpoint satisfies the applicable frozen task/evaluation contract on eligible separated data, with actual scoring, population/uncertainty and failure conditions. The current accepted evaluator shapes are not executed competence. No new arbitrary threshold is invented here.

The selected Ember checkpoint proposes a concrete useful change; assigned owners realize and independently assess it with comparative evidence and existing correctness/resource/recovery requirements. A change written by our seats cannot be labeled model-proposed merely because it was intended for Ember.

native_decision_contract.minimum: The harness consumes current model/run/data/resource state, determines which already-authorized actions are eligible, selects or proposes an action, executes it through the owned operation interface, evaluates the actual outcome, and records the next decision. It keeps a reason and evidence for both action and inaction.
native_decision_contract.first_demonstration: A real request leads from observation through one appropriate allowed tool/operation to an evaluated terminal outcome without hand-authored dispatch. Record which choice was deterministic policy and which was produced by the selected Ember checkpoint; do not call a fixed scheduler learned decision-making.
native_decision_contract.usefulness: For a consequential choice, name the expected benefit, comparator or prior state, and measured result. For model-proposed development, preserve proposal/checkpoint identity, resulting diff and accepted before/after evidence. Existing evaluation and independent-review ownership applies.
native_decision_contract.tool_boundary: Typed data/source, training, inference, evaluation and development operations share one service. Existing owner/resource/rights/custody permissions remain effective; an interface exposes no new approval or execution authority.
native_decision_contract.prohibited_inference: Do not use another teacher model for Ember inference, evaluation, selection or stopping, and do not count seat-authored output as evidence of Ember competence. Deterministic tools remain bound in the trace. No training data may come from our seats or a model any of us runs.
